newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SGL Carbon eyes double-digit growth.
newsitem.headline: German SGL Carbon eyes double-digit growth.

text.p: German SGL Carbon AG on Thursday set its sights on double-digit growth rates for 1997, after delivering strong 1996 results despite sluggish economic conditions.
"Barring any unforseen circumstances, we expect to post double-digit profit growth with profits growing more quickly than sales," SGL Carbon chief executive Robert Koehler told a news conference.

SGL Carbon, the world's largest carbon and graphite maker producing a range of products for the electrical, steel and semiconductor inustries, reported a 25 percent increase in operating profit to 324 million marks ($191.2 million) and a 13 percent increase in sales to 1.78 billion marks.

Despite a slump in the steel industry, which helped dent nine month sales, Koehler said SGL Carbon recovered strongly, posting record fourth quarter results with 485 million marks in sales and 93 million marks in operating profit.

Shareholders, who have seen their investment appreciate by over 300 percent since SGL Carbon first floated its shares in spring 1995, were rewarded with a 32 percent increase in the dividend to 2.20 marks.
On Thursday however investors took profits, sending the SGL Carbon shares down 3.6 percent to 221 marks.
Looking ahead, Koehler said he would prefer to let shareholders benefit even more in the company's strong results by buying back shares, once the German government permits this.
After acquisitions and higher prices, as well as improved currency relations, helped SGL Carbon post strong results, the group said it was not eyeing any large takeovers in the near future.

"We are still on the acquisitions trail but we don't have anything big going at the moment," Koehler told journalists, adding however that a few smaller ventures, to be financed from the group's cash flow, might be possible.
Such smaller deals could be conducted in the specialty graphite area, Koehler said, adding "these things would cost us 100 to 150 million marks and we could easily finance this."
Earlier this year SGL Carbon spent 80 million marks to acquire U.K. group RK Carbon, U.S. group M.G.P. and certain activities from German group Elektrokohle Lichtenberg.

The Wiesbaden-based group also said it would ask its shareholders at the annual meeting on April 21 to allow the group to issue warrant and/or convertible bonds for a volume of up to 300 million marks with a maturity of up to 10 years.

Shareholders would also be asked to approve additional capital connected with the issue of warrants or convertible bonds with a total nominal volume of up to 10 million marks or up to two million new shares.
Part of the authorised capital would be used to fulfil some incentive programmes for senior managers in the company.
This year, Koehler said SGL Carbon would benefit from an expected economic recovery in the steel industry, ongoing cost-cuttings and price adjustments in the carbon and graphite business area.
Koehler said he expected ongoing restructurings to cost the group about 25 million marks.
